tier_reason: Upgraded from C. The README tables come from the public test_sfft3.c, which times SFFT3 against FFTW's own fftwf_plan_dft_r2c_3d/c2r_3d in one binary, with the exact command lines shown. The makefile gives the compiler and flags (gcc -O3 -march=native -mtune=native -fopenmp -flto=auto -fno-schedule-insns), and both CPUs are named (Ryzen 7 3700X, i7-6700K). The gcc and FFTW versions are not stated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 8-core Ryzen 3700X, both FFTW_PATIENT: 512^3 8.428e-2 s vs FFTW3-P 1.009e-1 s (1.20x, derived from page data); 1024^3 7.733e-1 vs 1.011 s (1.31x, derived); 1024x1024x256 1.825e-1 vs 2.022e-1 s; 256^3 1.112e-2 vs 1.213e-2 s; slower at 64^3 (1.821e-4 vs 1.185e-4 s) and 128^3 (1.060e-3 vs 7.054e-4 s). 4-core i7-6700K, both FFTW_MEASURE: 512^3 0.182 vs 0.196 s (1.08x, derived), 1024^3 1.640 vs 1.705 s (1.04x, derived), 2048x2048x1024 7.360 vs 8.092 s (run separately with --nofftw/--nosfft); slower at 128^3, 256^3, 512x256x128 and 2100x2100x121.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc (version not stated), makefile: -O3 -march=native -mtune=native -DNDEBUG -fopenmp -std=gnu11 -fno-schedule-insns, linked with -flto=auto against pkg-config fftw3f and -lfftw3f_omp; i7 run adds CFLAGS=-DSFFT3_L2=256000. FFTW version not stated (Ubuntu system package via pkg-config).
corrections.workload: Average time of a forward plus reverse in-place 3-D real FFT in single precision (float, fftw3f), from 64^3 to 2100x2100x121 (and 2048x2048x1024), one OpenMP thread per physical core, padding and planning time excluded; SFFT3 uses FFTW's 1-D routines with cache-blocked transposes and a per-thread workspace.
corrections.caveats: The author calls it an untested proof of concept, run on two similar machines, and does not expect the results to generalize. Wins are 4-31% on large cubes, with losses at small sizes (and at four of nine sizes on the i7). SFFT3 uses a larger workspace than FFTW's 3-D routines, which the author says makes the timings not directly comparable. Single precision only. The gcc and FFTW versions are not stated. The README says it linked -lfftw3d_omp, but the makefile links -lfftw3f_omp.

notes: Numbers verified. GPL-3.0, 0 stars, last commit 2025-08-29, stale, all confirmed. Upgraded to A on the makefile-plus-named-CPU precedent; single precision added to workload.

tier_reason: The README gives first-party percentages against CMSIS-DSP arm_cfft_radix2_q31 with compilers, -O3 and the MCU (Kinetis K20). The public main.c harness (FTM0 cycle counter, 100 runs) times only SYLT's fft_inverse; there is no CMSIS call or raw cycle count in public code, so not A.

corrections.license: MHG (Moral High Ground) license: the Unlicense text released 'under the single condition that good moral standards are maintained in its use', plus non-binding requests; custom, not an OSI/SPDX license (the README calls it GPL-compatible)
corrections.caveats: One data point (256-point inverse) against the 2014 CMSIS-DSP 1.4.2 library, which predates later CMSIS FFT routines (arm_cfft_q31). Only percentages are published, no cycle counts. The public harness main.c (FRDM-K20D50M, FTM0 cycle counter) times only SYLT's fft_inverse; the CMSIS side is not in the repo. License is the custom MHG text: the Unlicense plus a vague 'good moral standards' condition, so it is non-standard and treated as reference. A forward-FFT DIT math error was fixed in Jan 2021. 'Designed for optimal performance, not optimal accuracy'; inputs must be scaled to avoid overflow.
